topic: Can the April 1, 2026 occupant change reset the rent to market?
value: NO - an original occupant still resides in the unit
detail: Sec. 37.3(d)(2)(B) excludes a 'partial change[] in occupancy ... where one or more of the occupants ... remains an occupant in lawful possession'. Rule 6.14 / Costa-Hawkins market-rate increases require ALL original occupants to have vacated. Sec. 37.3(a)(11)(A) separately bars any increase imposed solely because an occupant was added. sf.gov: 'Landlords in San Francisco cannot charge more rent simply because a new roommate ... has moved into a unit.'

topic: Does a new lease with a continuing original occupant remove rent control?
value: NO - rent increase limitations continue for the duration of the new tenancy
detail: Sec. 37.3(d)(1)(A)(ii): where the preceding tenancy was terminated by a 1946.1 notice or a change in terms noticed under Civil Code 827, 'the rent increase limitation provisions of Chapter 37 shall continue to apply for the duration of the new tenancy in that dwelling or unit.' Civil Code 1954.53(a)(1) is consistent.

topic: Notice required if banked increases are imposed (13.1% or 11.7%)
value: 90 days' written notice (+5 days if mailed); notice must identify the banked portion and the years/dates
detail: Both scenarios exceed 10%, triggering Civil Code 827(b)(3)(A) and sf.gov's 90-day rule. Sec. 37.3(b)(1) / Rule 4.10(a)(1) / Rule 4.12(b) require the banked breakdown and dates. Nonconforming increases are null and void.

If the increase is effective on a date other than June 1, a skipped year's increase can be permanently lost, per the Rent Board's own worked example, and the effective date becomes the new anniversary date. Also, an effective date on/after March 1, 2027 would require the unpublished 2027-28 rate. No date is filled in here - flagged for manual decision.

topic: What is 'reasonable and normal' under official sources
value: The published annual allowable increase (1.6% for 3/1/2026-2/28/2027), applied once per 12 months on base rent, with a current license and correct written notice
detail: ANALYSIS: this is the only increase that official sources describe as available without a petition or approval, and it is the same for every covered unit in the City regardless of ZIP code. Larger banked increases are lawful only if calculated exactly right and correctly noticed, and they are the most likely to be challenged. Any figure above the published rate requires a Rent Board petition and approval.
